provenance.who: a coding-agent session (coordinator), from speeds-kit docs/TAPGRADE.md ('the chain') and userscripts/tapgrade.user.js, TapGrade 0.6.6; steps checked against the code by a second, independent reader
provenance.note: Written from what the 0.6.6 code and its mock-Canvas audit do, not from a person using it on a phone: nobody has run this on real Canvas yet. Amounts and similarities are guesses. Judgments: (1) at Apply the comment text of a change is built only when a student is opened, so the first COMMIT of each chain says everything_on_screen false and the colocation verifier fires there; (2) Apply is irreversible (TapGrade has no undo; the text from before stays on the phone), Resume and Retry failed are idempotent (they write only what still differs); (3) docs/TAPGRADE.md called the tap on Update Canvas after a refresh a RE-ORIENT, kept in tapgrade-0.6.6-interrupted-lands-on-grade; (4) the held item 'what to expect' is the person's own cross-check: the screen already shows 212 rows and 66 students, but the block that shows 212 scrolls away while the foot shows only 66. (5) After speeds-kit PR #33 got the reload fix (the page comes back on Update Canvas while an update is open: audit VIEW-1, VIEW-2), tapgrade-0.6.6-interrupted was edited to match, from the audit check, by the session that made the fix: its REFRESH restores position and the RE-ORIENT step is gone. The chain as it was is kept as tapgrade-0.6.6-interrupted-lands-on-grade. That edit has not been read by a second reader. The removal of older summary comments (the 'Removed 18 of 54' flow of HW1, its own confirm and its own retry) is not modelled.

chains.task: The HW1 correction pass with TapGrade 0.6.6, nothing goes wrong: apply 66 updates to Canvas and see them verified
chains.setup: Once, on a computer: `python3 -m speedkit.tapgrade <hw> --userscript --corrections <file> --out hw-data.user.js`, the file put next to TapGrade. Not part of the chain: nothing on the phone is picked by hand.
chains.notes: Step 6 is optional in the app; the chain is the careful path. Peak working set is 3 (the step's own need plus 2 held), which is exactly B. The one finding is at step 7: the comment text of a change is one tap away, not on the screen.
